Sports.title: Paul Gascoigne tears up on live TV - as he reveals his alcohol addiction was so bad he drank 30 cans of Red Bull a day to wean himself off booze
Sports.content:
Consider yourself a World Cup expert? Challenge yourself with our exclusive quiz for free by signing up to our World Cup newsletter. Get it HERE

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Paul Gascoigne almost broke down in tears during an emotional live TV appearance on Wednesday morning, discussing his alcohol addiction.

'Gazza', 59, has been open about his struggles and spoke to Ed Balls and Suzanna Reid on Good Morning Britain, tearing up when speaking about how his new book could save lives.

The England football legend's new autobiography called 'Eight' is about the turmoil away from the pitch, his addiction and recovery.

He said: 'This is probably the happiest I've been in five years. Just in general, I've got the book coming out, excited about that. Things are up.

'When I played football, you knew what you were doing from Monday until Monday.

'Now when you wake up on a Monday, you think, "what am I gonna do?". But things are looking up and I'm quite happy.

Paul Gascoigne almost broke down in tears during his appearance on Good Morning Britain

'If it saves someone's life then I'm happy.'



Paul 'Gazza' Gascoigne gets emotional as he talks about his new book and how he's the happiest he's been in years. pic.twitter.com/CrpN57CSX3 — Good Morning Britain (@GMB) June 10, 2026

'This book is not about football, it's different. A lot of people have told me they've read it and said it's saved their life.'

The former midfielder's voice wobbled as he added: 'If that book can save one person's life then I've done my job.'

'Every morning, I don't think about tomorrow. I just try to keep it in the day.

'Some days I find it hard. I just think, 'right, work on that today' and I get through the day.

'I know too many addicts have died each week. When people come up to you and say the book has helped them, it means a lot.

'I've learnt a lot. I used to wake up and think, 'what's wrong with me today?' It used to be a big battle every day I woke up. Now I have a coffee and plan the day ahead.'

Gascoigne, who is one of England's best loved players and starred for Newcastle, Tottenham, Everton, Lazio, Middlesbrough and Rangers, also said he suffered such horrendous withdrawal symptoms when quitting alcohol that he ended up drinking 30 cans of Red Bull every day.

He continued: 'I went to the gym and I needed a few Red Bulls. I was tired so I needed a few more.

'Then I had some more and eventually I was having 30 cans a day. I wasn't drinking and the withdrawal was horrific.

'I sat on a rock for four days and didn't move. I said good morning and goodnight, that's all I did.'

Gazza has experienced a number of health scares over the years, the most recent of which he spoke about in January.

The England legend has struggled with alcohol addiction and mental health problems in the wake of his retirement from football (pictured at Euro 96)

He made the revelation on the podcast Clutch 9 and admitted he had been 'panicking' and 's****ing' himself due to the pain as he was treated in hospital.

'I was hanging something up and I fell backwards. I broke six ribs and I punctured a couple of lungs,' said Gascoigne.

'I go to the hospital and I'm in agony obviously and they give me some pain relief. I just felt my neck getting bigger. I got the surgeon in quickly because I was panicking.

'I could see my dad in the clouds and I was really panicking. I've had 38 operations so this normally doesn't bother me, but this time I was really s****ing myself.

'I was saying, "please get the surgeon". I was crying my eyes out.'

Gascoigne, who won 57 caps for the Three Lions and is regarded as one of the country’s most gifted players of all time was found collapsed in the bedroom of his home in Poole, Dorset, last July.

He had been discovered by his close friend and personal assistant Steve Foster and was stabilised after being found to have been struggling with a throat condition, before later being released.

Sports.title: Lionel Messi and Argentina team-mates have passport details LEAKED in bizarre team sheet data breach
Sports.content:
Lionel Messi and his Argentina team-mates were involved in a bizarre data breach before a pre-World Cup friendly that saw their passport details accidentally leaked.

Lionel Scaloni's side beat Iceland 3-0 in Alabama in the early hours of Wednesday morning (GMT) in front of 88,000 fans.

When countries submit team sheets ahead of kick off, these sometimes include passport numbers of their players, although that private information is normally blurred out or deleted before being shared to the media.

However, Argentina's team sheet - which included Messi, Chelsea star Enzo Fernandez and Man United's Lisandro Martinez - was released with their passport numbers still on there, and this was reproduced by several local media outlets.

This damaging security leak therefore exposed the details for the entire Argentina starting XI and substitutes.

The error appeared to be the responsibility of Road to '26, the Turkish Airlines-sponsored company who were in charge of organising the friendly. They have arranged multiple other pre-tournament games in the USA too.

Lionel Messi and his Argentina team-mates were involved in a bizarre data breach before a pre-World Cup friendly that saw their passport details accidentally leaked

Iceland didn't include the passport numbers of their players on their team sheet, so they managed to avoid a similar leak.

During the match, Messi scored a penalty shortly after coming off the bench in the 70th minute.

Valentin Barco earlier put Scaloni's side ahead in the first half, before Thiago Almada then made it 3-0 late on.

Speaking after the game, Messi - who had picked up a hamstring injury last month when playing for Inter Miami - provided an update on his own fitness and hopes for Argentina this summer.

'I’m happy, enjoying every moment, and excited as always,' he said. 'I felt really good.

'I wanted to get going and shake off the lingering fears that come with an injury - to be able to play freely.

'We have a week left to get everyone in top shape and be ready for the opener.'

Messi played a huge role in Argentina's World Cup triumph in 2022 and they have also won the last two Copa America titles.

This time around the reigning champions face Algeria, Jordan and Austria in their group, with their first game coming next Wednesday against the North African side.

Sports.title: Lionel Messi's Argentina swansong and Cristiano Ronaldo gunning for glory with Portugal: The football superstars who will see out their last dance at the 2026 World Cup
Sports.content:
Lionel Messi's Argentina swansong and Cristiano Ronaldo gunning for glory with Portugal: The football superstars who will see out their last dance at the 2026 World Cup

Consider yourself a World Cup expert? Challenge yourself with our exclusive quiz for free by signing up to our World Cup newsletter. Get it HERE

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

The 2026 World Cup is on the horizon, with the opening game set to take place on Thursday as Mexico welcome South Africa in the opener of the 23rd edition of football's greatest tournament.

The stage is set and for many young players it is a chance to shine. However, this year's global tournament will also serve as a curtain call for some of football's biggest stars.

Among those set to play at their last World Cup finals this summer are Premier League greats, titans of the international game, and even former World Cup winners.

Here, Daily Mail Sport waves farewell to some of the greatest players to play the game in their last dance at international level.

Cristiano Ronaldo (Portugal)

Number of World Cups played: 5

First World Cup appearance: Angola vs Portugal, June 11 2006

A hero for many football lovers across the planet, Cristiano Ronaldo will play in his sixth World Cup boasting an impressive record alongside Guillermo Ochoa and Lionel Messi as the only players to have featured in six or more World Cups.

Cristiano Ronaldo will be looking to go out on a high at this summer's World Cup in America

The 41-year-old made his debut at the finals a staggering 20 years ago and has been a fixture in the side at every tournament since

The Portuguese phenomenon has notched eight goals and provided two assists in 22 appearances in this tournament and became the first and only player in history to score in five different World Cup campaigns in Qatar 2022.

Dubbed by international teammate Bruno Fernandes as, 'the best striker in the world, and the greatest player in football history,' it is clear for all to see the lasting impact Ronaldo has left at both international and club level. Yet still, many critics highlight the 41-year-old's ego as a threat to his nation's chances of going far in the tournament.

Despite the outside noise, Ronaldo will yet again lead his country in their opening game a week from now against the Democratic Republic of Congo who feature in their first tournament since 1974.

If Portugal are to have a say in the outcome of the 2026 World Cup, make no mistake that Ronaldo will have something to do with it. A grandstand finish looks on the cards for Portugal's main man.

Lionel Messi (Argentina)

Number of World Cups played: 5

First World Cup appearance: Argentina vs Serbia and Montenegro, June 16 2006

After the incredible finish to the 2022 World Cup final in Qatar between Argentina and France, Lionel Messi finally got his hands on the trophy he had been chasing his whole career.

He teased the idea of retiring from international football before the campaign in 2022 saying, 'It's my last World Cup surely.' Four years later and the Argentine magician has remained in Lionel Scaloni's 26-man squad as they aim to become the first nation since 1962 to defend a World Cup title.

Lionel Messi achieved immortality in Argentina when he captained his side to their third World Cup victory in 2022

But there has been an injury scare for Messi ahead of this summer's tournament, with the 38-year-old having to be replaced in the 73rd minute of Inter Miami's 6-4 victory against Philadelphia Union just over two weeks ago. He was rested in Argentina's penultimate international friendly on the weekend against Honduras.

Messi holds the all-time leading appearance record in World Cups with 26. He has scored 13 goals and provided eight assists in these appearances and in Qatar he was involved in ten of his nation's 15 goals – a campaign that cemented him, as he has been so often throughout his career, as the man for the big occasion.

Argentina kickstart their tournament against Algeria in Kansas City next Wednesday. It is unclear yet whether Messi will feature against the Algerians, but one thing is for sure whether his minutes are limited or not: the superstar from Rosario has given generations of Argentinians hope that their country will win the World Cup for a fourth time.

Neymar Jr (Brazil)

Number of World Cups played: 3

First World Cup appearance: Brazil vs Croatia, June 12 2014

A man once affectionately labelled 'O Menino de Ouro' (the golden boy) by his boyhood club Santos has come a long way from the hardships he faced growing up in Sao Paolo.

Neymar has had an illustrious career and is celebrated as an icon across Brazil by fans - and even his international teammates - which is no surprise as to why his inclusion in the 2026 Brazil squad by Carlo Ancelotti was such a massive boost for his country.

For Brazilians, the name Neymar means more than just football. Neymar is a symbol of joy, creativity, flair and audacity and has made so many fall in love with watching him play. But the 34-year-old veteran has faced similar injury concerns as former Barcelona teammate Lionel Messi, with a calf problem keeping him out for the time being.

Neymar experienced his maiden World Cup on home soil in 2014 after missing out on selection four years earlier

An injury-troubled veteran Carlo Ancelotti hopes that the star will be a talismanic presence for the squad this summer

Whilst he may be sidelined for a portion of Brazil's group stage fixtures, his inclusion in the Selecao's 26-man squad sparked mini celebrations across the nation.

The all-time leading scorer for Brazil is not shy of putting on a performance and has grabbed headlines in previous tournaments ranging from his outrageous skills to his even more outrageous haircuts.

With injuries causing a stop-start season with Santos, all signs point to this being Neymar's last World Cup. Brazil will be hoping to give their man a perfect send off, winning the World Cup for the first time since 2002 in an attempt to repay their golden boy for everything he has given to them.

Luka Modric (Croatia)

Number of World Cups played: 4

First World Cup appearance: Japan vs Croatia, June 18 2006

Renowned for his elegant style of play and press resistance on the grandest of stages, few players embody the phrase 'aged like a fine wine' as Luka Modric does. Now playing his football in Italy for AC Milan the Croatian midfielder has typified what it means to be a true professional.

Modric scored what was perhaps his final goal on Croatian soil on Saturday in an international friendly against Slovenia. At 40 years old he is still the heartbeat of Croatia's side, and adored by many fans across the globe. Nicknamed 'The Maestro' he will feature in fifth World Cup this summer as Croatia take on England in their opening game.

Throughout his career, Modric has always been a very intelligent footballer, and this has allowed him to outclass his opposition, even when his legs get heavy, through timing and decision making. With 196 caps, no one has represented Croatia more than Modric has. His longevity and hunger to play is a true credit to who he is as an athlete and person.

Luka Modric has been a mainstay in the Croatian set-up and continues as one of their key stars

Modric will captain a side looking to hit the heights they hit in 2018, when they reached the World Cup final for the first time in their nation's history despite being beaten 4-1 by France. It looks unlikely that Modric will take part in another World Cup, and for football fans everywhere his name will live long in the memory for what he has achieved throughout his sparkling career.

Manuel Neuer (Germany)

Number of World Cups played: 4

First World Cup appearance: Germany vs Australia, June 14 2010

Julian Nagelsmann announced ahead of the 2026 World Cup that 40-year-old Manuel Neuer will be the first-choice keeper for Germany. Neuer has redefined what it means to be a goalkeeper in the modern day, often recognised for his ability to play out the back with his feet and act as another defender earning himself the nickname 'The Sweeper Keeper'.

Throughout his incredible career, Neuer has won 33 major professional trophies including 13 Bundesliga trophies, two UEFA Champions League trophies and - of course - the 2014 World Cup as Germany beat Argentina 1-0 thanks to a Mario Goetze goal deep into extra time. He also won the Golden Glove award in 2014 with four clean sheets in seven appearances.

After Germany's quarter-final defeat in the 2024 Euros to tournament winners Spain, Neuer announced that he would be retiring from international football. Now ahead of this summer's tournament, Nagelsmann intends to go all the way and has named the 'aura and quality' that Neuer brings to team as a big part of his optimism.

Manuel Neuer is one of only a handful of players at this World Cup featuring over the age of 40

Germany, as always, are strong contenders for the 2026 World Cup trophy and just like their success 12 years ago in Brazil, Neuer remains a huge part of the way the Germans build up their football from back to front as well as being an incredible shot-stopper.

His eventual retirement from international football will be a huge miss as he is widely regarded as one of the greatest goalkeepers to have ever played the game.

Mohamed Salah (Egypt)

Number of World Cups played: 1

First World Cup appearance: Russia vs Egypt, June 19 2018

The Egyptian King, Mohamed Salah, will play in his second World Cup tournament after making his debut back in 2018 in Russia. After a turbulent season at club level with Liverpool, Salah will be hoping to end his season on a high with the fifth-highest-ranking African side in the competition.

Salah will captain the Pharaohs against Belgium in their first game of the 2026 World Cup and has stated, 'we want to make people proud of us, and we will do our utmost.' The two-times African Player of the Year is aiming for his side to go further than any Egyptian team has gone in the tournament.

Turning 34 in a week's time, Salah has unfinished business on the world stage. He scored twice in his nation's campaign in Russia eight years ago but is still yet to taste a victory in the competition. He has been on the losing side twice in both 2017 and 2021 during the African Cup of Nations, but former captain Ahmed Fathi has backed him to 'achieve something with the Pharaohs at the 2026 World Cup'.

Despite having enjoying a heavily decorated playing career with Liverpool, Mohamed Salah has only featured at one World Cup

'He always made the difference, and I hope he will do it again in the United States', Fathi told AFP.

With his move away from Liverpool at the end of this season, there is no denying that this is likely to be Salah's last involvement in a World Cup. The king of Egypt has brought joy to so many of his admirers throughout his decorated career and is a beacon of pride for many Africans.

James Rodriguez (Colombia)

Number of World Cups played: 3

First World Cup appearance: Colombia vs Greece, June 14 2014

When we talk about the World Cup, it is hard to forget the delicious strike a 22-year-old James Rodriguez scored in Brazil in 2014 in the round of 16 against Uruguay. Brazuca plucked out of the air, controlled on his chest, left-footed volley, crossbar and in. A goal to take your breath away and Rodriguez will always be a part of international folklore because of the magic he provided that night in Rio.

His inclusion in Colombia's 2026 World Cup squad marks his third global tournament and is considered by many as his last. The 34-year-old departed MLS side Minnesota United so he could focus solely on his preparations for the 2026 World Cup.

Rodriguez, together with Bayern Munich's Luis Diaz, contributed to 17 of Colombia's 28 goals in World Cup qualifying. He comes alive when playing for Colombia and was named player of the tournament in their 2024 Copa America campaign despite losing by one goal to nil against Argentina in the final.

James Rodriguez burst into international consciousness with his stunning appearance at the World Cup in Brazil 12 years ago

Despite facing many injury problems throughout his career, the Colombian is often viewed as the face of his nation's football team. Sitting just four assists off Carlos Valderrama's record, there is no doubt the midfielder will be keen to etch his name into Colombian football history in what will be his final act on the World stage.

Riyad Mahrez (Algeria)

Number of World Cups played: 1

First World Cup appearance: Belgium vs Algeria, June 17 2014

If you cast your mind back to the 2015-16 Premier League season, Riyad Mahrez is a man who knows the true meaning of defying the odds. An inspiration for many Algerians, Mahrez has remained elegant and dangerous despite his increasing age.

After failing to qualify for the 2018 and 2022 World Cup campaigns, Algeria come into this tournament as Africa's fourth highest rank side. Mahrez will captain his nation as they take on the holders Argentina in their first game. The 35-year-old is undoubtedly the one to watch for his country who have strong ambitions of progressing to the knockout round of the competition.

Riyad Mahrez has scarcely played World Cup football but will enjoy his swansong with Algeria on the biggest stage this summer

He has already made the statement that this World Cup will be his last and in an open training session at the Nelson-Mandela stadium in Baraki, Mahrez and his international teammates saluted the Algerian supporters for the last time before they travelled to North America.

Contributing to 75 goals in 113 appearances, the Al-Ahli winger has been a true servant to his nation. Mahrez will be hoping to leave his mark at this tournament, guiding his team into the knockout stages as they did in 2014 where they were unpicked by Germany. Mahrez has changed the way football is played in Algeria and will undoubtedly go down as one of the most talented African players of all time.

Sports.title: World Cup referee who was kicked out of America - after being flagged for TERRORISM fears according to Trump officials - gets hero's welcome back in Somalia
Sports.content:
Consider yourself a World Cup expert? Challenge yourself with our exclusive quiz for free by signing up to our World Cup newsletter. Get it HERE

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

The Somalian referee acclaimed as the 'best in Africa' - who was kicked out of the US ahead of the World Cup - was given a hero's welcome in his homeland.

Omar Abdulkadir Artan, 34, was dropped from FIFA's list for the tournament after the American authorities refused him permission to enter the country at Miami International Airport.

The Trump administration claimed he was turned away due to 'terrorism fears' in a shocking turn of events that has caused a major outcry and support for the referee who expressed his bitter disappointment at the rejection.

He said the decision had shattered his 'biggest dream' of officiating at a World Cup.

Artan was put on a flight to Turkey and then back home to Somalia where he was greeted with plenty of fanfare.

He was filmed stepping off the plane and being mobbed by well-wishers and dignitaries, shaking hands and smiling broadly.

World Cup referee Omar Abdulkadir Artan was given a hero's welcome back in Somalia

The referee then posed for photos while holding up the Somalian flag in a show of national pride and defiance.

His exclusion from the World Cup has been a major talking point ahead of the tournament kicking off on Thursday.

Speaking to the New York Times, Artan insisted he was 'very disappointed' in the decision, adding: 'I had the right papers and everything. I had the right visa.'

However, the Trump administration made a bombshell claim that the referee was denied entry due to terrorism fears.

In a statement provided to FOX, a Trump official said: 'This individual was seeking admission to the United States.

'Upon further inspection by CBP, derogatory information, including association with suspected members of terror organizations, was discovered making the traveler ineligible for admission to the United States under the Immigration and Nationality Act (INA).

'The traveler was refused admission and given immigration forms that provide the section of law used to complete an expedited removal under 8235 of the INA.

'President Trump's administration will not allow any security threat to enter our country - full stop.'

Previously, US Customs and Border Protection had said in a statement: 'The traveler underwent additional inspection, a routine part of C.B.P.'s inspection process when officers need to verify information or determine admissibility.

Somalis hold pictures of Artan, who had been expected to officiate matches at the 2026 FIFA World Cup but was refused entry to the United States, during a match in Somalia on Tuesday

'Following inspection, the traveler, a referee for the FIFA World Cup, was determined to be inadmissible due to vetting concerns and was denied entry.'

FIFA initially confirmed last week that Artan's visa situation had been 'fully resolved and he will now be available to officiate at the FIFA World Cup'.

But on Monday night the governing body released a statement, reading: 'FIFA can confirm that match official Omar Abdulkadir Artan will be unable to train and officiate at the FIFA World Cup 2026 after he was denied entry into the United States.

'FIFA is not involved in host country immigration processes, including visa adjudications, and has been informed by authorities that Mr Artan's status will not be changed at present.'

'In line with previous FIFA events, a host government ultimately determines who receives a visa and who is admitted into their country.'

Meanwhile, when discussing the matter with the New York Times, Artan said: 'I am very, very disappointed. I'm just simply a referee who's trying to live his dream, the biggest dream of my life, to come to the World Cup.'

The Somali official also claimed that he also showed documentation from FIFA and photographs of his career as a professional referee to border officials.

They also checked online material about his career, said Artan - who was named referee of the year in 2025 by the Confederation of African Football.

The official claims his immigration interview ended after 11 hours, before he was taken to a separate holding cell. He was detained there for several more hours before being put on a flight back to Istanbul, despite officials not giving him a reason for denying him entry to the US.

Somalia features on President Donald Trump's travel ban list and last month he said of Somali immigrants in America: 'They're all crooks.'

The Trump administration has claimed that Artan was denied entry into the US due to alleged terrorism fears. President Trump pictured with the President of FIFA, Gianni Infantino, last July

In January he called the nation 'the worst country in the world'.

The United States has refused to issue visas to some members of Iran's staff for the World Cup.

Iran players landed in Mexico at the weekend and the entire squad were pictured disembarking from their plane with pins on their clothing bearing the number 168, a reference to the number of people killed by what was believed to be a US missile in February.

Last week Iraqi World Cup star Aymen Hussein was held and questioned for almost seven hours after arriving at Chicago's O'Hare Airport.

He was eventually allowed to enter, along with the rest of the Iraq squad, but the team's photographer was barred from entering the country.

Sports.title: BBC director of sport defends controversial work-from-home World Cup plans and confirms Gabby Logan to anchor the final
Sports.content:
BBC director of sport defends controversial work-from-home World Cup plans and confirms Gabby Logan to anchor the final

Consider yourself a World Cup expert? Challenge yourself with our exclusive quiz for free by signing up to our World Cup newsletter. Get it HERE

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Dusk descends over New York at the flick of a switch more than 3,000 miles away in Salford. As the time of day changes on the giant LED screen that forms a backdrop to the BBC’s World Cup studio, so too does the lighting in here.

Then, suddenly, we’re in Boston. It’s a clear day but that can be altered easily enough to match the actual conditions there.

With a press of a button, the desk where Gabby Logan, Wayne Rooney, Micah Richards and Olivier Giroud will be sat when the BBC’s live coverage kicks off with the Canada-Bosnia game on Thursday night, rises to waist height.

The backdrop changes again and now we’re on the ‘terrace’, a more laid-back vibe where Logan and the pundits can stand or sit casually on stools. Fans create a breeze to give the impression they are outside.

Welcome to the BBC’s coverage of the 2026 World Cup. Rather than having a main studio in the host country, as the corporation has at previous tournaments, and basing their presenters and pundits abroad, Auntie has gone for the comforts of home.

That could change after the quarter-final stage, as Daily Mail Sport revealed in December. And, yes, there will be commentary teams in the stadium for the majority of the 54 matches being broadcast live by the BBC, reporters embedded with the England and Scotland camps, and other journalists dotted around North America chasing the big stories in conjunction with a team working around the clock at home.

The BBC have invested heavily in a state-of-the-art studio, which features a giant panoramic screen

BBC director of sport Alex Kay-Jelski has defended the decision base their coverage of the 2026 World Cup from Salford

But for the most part, the decision was taken to work out of this state-of-the-art studio in Salford to save millions of licence fee money. With the tournament finally upon us, the BBC’s director of sport Alex Kay-Jelski is happy with the decision.

‘Right now, I'm incredibly happy with it,’ he says. ‘To have what would probably be an extra couple of hundred people out there – and that's before you build a studio – you’re talking millions.

‘If I was standing here saying everything is going to be done from a studio in Dallas, you would rightly be saying to me, “how can you justify that expense?”.

‘I don't think the answer from a financial sustainable point of view is to say everyone can go. I don't think that is a very clever way of me to spend licence fee money.’

Kay-Jelski is taking Daily Mail Sport on a tour of the operation, explaining how it will all work.

The studio, he explains, will have benefits beyond the World Cup with some of the LED technology set to be introduced next season to Match of the Day which is filmed in a smaller studio and has been relying on older ‘green screen’ technology.

We start in the main production gallery where the director, editor, production co-ordinator, vision mixer, resource manager, and a team of graphics and virtual studio operators sit on two banks of desks facing a wall of screens. With the sound crew next door, there are up to 30 of them at any one time.

From here, they can blend the studio footage with computer-generated 360-degree cityscapes for the 16 host venues with variants for day, dusk and night, as well as dynamic weather effects. Augmented reality as opposed to virtual reality.

The studio will have benefits beyond the World Cup with some of the LED technology set to be introduced next season to Match of the Day, which is filmed in a smaller studio

Inside one of the eight edit suites used to produce highlights and the clips, which the pundits need to illustrate their analysis

BBC presenters and pundits will work in their Salford studio until the quarter-final stage of the tournament

A short walk brings us to the VT hub which will record 44 lines from the international broadcast centre in Dallas, including 14 lines from each game with footage of the action from every angle.

The eight edit suites here are used to produce highlights and the clips which the pundits need to illustrate their analysis. That involves a particularly quick turnaround at half-time when the BBC don’t have the benefit of a commercial break like ITV.

Then there are unforeseen circumstances that could disrupt the operation, not least the threat of storms in the US which may cause kick-offs to be significantly delayed or matches held up, creating the nightmare scenario of games overlapping.

The BBC face an early challenge this weekend with its live broadcast of Brazil versus Morocco on Saturday night closely followed by Haiti versus Scotland in the early hours of Sunday.

Back in the new studio, the impressive backdrop is complemented by an LED floor in front of the presenter and pundits, which they can’t see and looks a little distorted to the human eye anyway, but comes to life for the TV viewers at home when filmed by the cameras above.

Former Match of the Day presenter Gary Lineker aimed a dig at his old employers in April, saying that he was looking forward to watching the World Cup from Times Square instead of ‘in Salford in a green box’.

‘It’s not a green box in Salford,’ Kay-Jelski retorted. ‘It’s a beautiful state-of-the-art studio. No one’s seen it until now. It’s completely fine to assume that what was there before was what it was going to be – and I’m really proud of this. It’s not a big deal.’

As well as the BBC’s 54 live games, all 104 matches can be accessed over its digital platforms – iPlayer, 5Live, BBC Sounds, the BBC Sport website and app.

In an attempt to reach out to new and younger viewers, there will be content on TikTok and the first 10 minutes of some live games will be broadcast on the new BBC Sport Football YouTube channel.

‘I think it's quite a clever way of putting the games in front of people who aren't obsessed with football and who aren't sitting there with their day-by-day planner,’ says Kay-Jelski.

‘Again, we'll see what works and what doesn't, but I actually think it seems pretty clever and interesting.’

Sports.title: Elliot Anderson is at the heart of a Manchester transfer war and indispensable for Thomas Tuchel - the reserved England star's rise is one nobody saw coming, writes IAN LADYMAN
Sports.content:
Elliot Anderson says he cannot remember where he watched the last major tournament that England played in, the 2024 European Championships in Germany.

‘I definitely would have watched it,’ he told me sheepishly earlier this year.

‘I will have been with my mates somewhere.’

Life has moved quickly for the Nottingham Forest midfielder recently. The journey from his friend’s sofa to the heart of the England midfield here in America was one nobody really saw coming.

But now that he is here – now that he is one of a group of players England manager Thomas Tuchel knows he can’t be without - it feels as though the challenges may only really be beginning.

Anderson is something of a poster boy for the Premier League’s financial rules and regulations. The face of PSR, you may say.

Elliot Anderson has rapidly become indispensable for Thomas Tuchel's England side

His move from Newcastle to Forest two summers ago only happened because the north-east club had to sell a home-grown talent to balance their books.

His next transfer is likely to be easier to understand. Both Manchester clubs are willing to pay big money this summer to make Anderson the player around whom a midfield can be built. Currently, City are favourites and the chances are he will wear sky blue next season.

Forest will not lie down and roll over. It’s not the way owner Evangelos Marinakis does business and the Greek is already known to be irritated by the assumption that his best player can be picked off at will by one of the two northern powerhouses.

So this is one that could drag on into the start of this World Cup and that will bring its own pressures to bear on a player of whom an awful lot is already being asked here in America.

Tuchel has already made his own stance on the matter clear. Unlike some of his predecessors, he will not ask his players to leave their club business at the door of this tournament. He knows that is not realistic.

'If anyone has the chance to complete a transfer, we will not stand in the way, but it has to align with our schedule and our goals, which is to be focused and prepare for matches,’ said Tuchel.

‘The last day before the match and the second last day, not.

'Until now, no player approached me. The doctor is ready to take any medical if needed! We are always happy to help to have clarity around the player.'

It’s a grown-up approach from a manager who likes to treat his players as adults and is acutely aware of how the world works. As a former coach at clubs like Chelsea, PSG and Bayern, the German knows that the transfer market doesn’t press pause just because there is a World Cup on.

Anderson (left), pictured with Harry Kane, Reece James, Djed Spence and Morgan Rogers, is at the centre of a transfer battle between the Manchester clubs

Anderson, 23, is aware of the situation, of course. He knows that Forest have already knocked one £80m bid back from City. His representatives, meanwhile, are currently at that stage where they can sit back and let the clubs get on with it.

‘Elliot won’t be fazed by it,’ explains one source who knows him well.

‘He isn’t that kind of lad.

‘The move from Newcastle to Forest was huge. He envisaged staying at Newcastle for ever.

‘But when the move came out of the blue, he just walked out of the door and got on with it.’

Anderson is a reserved character. He is not hugely excitable. He still remains unconvinced that he is the most famous member of his family. His brother Wil was a contestant on Love Island.

‘When he went into the show I was playing for Newcastle and when he came out I was at Forest,’ Anderson told me.

‘I think he took longer to get his head round than I did.’

It’s quite possible that a similar story may play out this summer. City, in particular, do not seem intent on waiting for Anderson’s value to go up on the back of a good World Cup. They want to do a deal quickly.

Having lost his mother in mid-April, this has already been a difficult spell for Anderson and the responsibility he will carry here for Tuchel’s England is significant.

But this is a young man who knows his own mind. For example, he is not ashamed to say that one of his key footballing mentors is the disgraced Joey Barton. Anderson played for Barton on loan at Bristol Rovers and flourished. Told he would have to wait to get in his team, a teenage Anderson vowed to prove him wrong. It took him a week.

In the build up to England’s last two tournaments – the 2024 Euros and winter World Cup of 2022 – Tuchel’s predecessor Gareth Southgate fretted about the lack of a natural partner for Rice in his midfield.

Anderson is a reserved but fiercely determined character ready to take to the big stage

‘It’s always a question of Declan and who?’ was Southgate’s most memorable quote on the matter.

The last Euros saw Trent Alexander-Arnold and Conor Gallagher – remember them? – thrust to the fore. Eventually Southgate settled on United’s precocious youngster Kobbie Mainoo.

Mainoo is in Tuchel’s squad here and if United got their way he would partner Anderson in a new Old Trafford midfield next season.

It will be Rice and Anderson in America for England, though. Tuchel and his assistant Anthony Barry have privately described the latter as the ‘gift that fell from the sky’, such was Anderson’s emergence from almost nowhere on their watch.

Anderson – who used to wear a Lionel Messi shirt in the back garden - may not remember much about the summer of 2024. The summer of 2026 will leave a greater impression, with club and with country.

Sports.title: Steamy new photos catch Kim Kardashian's intimate moment with Lewis Hamilton... as insiders reveal cruel whispers of jealous WAGs
Sports.content:
Steamy new photos catch Kim Kardashian's intimate moment with Lewis Hamilton... as insiders reveal cruel whispers of jealous WAGs

Kim Kardashian's polarizing entrance into the world of Formula One this weekend has sent the rumor mill into overdrive across one of the world's most ego-driven sports.

The reality star, 45, didn't just upset the regulars in the F1 paddock in Monaco, her first F1 race, by dismissing popular reporter Martin Brundle when he tried to interview her before the race began - an incident angry insiders have branded 'classless.'

In the F1 WAG world, Kardashian's presence is already resetting the power order. Some are in their own race to be as friendly with her as possible while others, the Daily Mail can reveal, are unhappy at being upstaged so dramatically.

Kardashian watched boyfriend Lewis Hamilton, 41, race for Ferrari with Alexandra Leclerc, the wife of Hamilton's fellow driver and teammate, Charles. And after Hamilton finished second, Kardashian joined him on his luxury yacht, alongside sister Khloe, to celebrate off the coast of the French Riviera.

The Daily Mail's pictures show the new power couple hugging and kissing in the evening sun. Kardashian had changed out of her dress while Hamilton was still in his red Ferrari polo shirt and cap.

But after Kardashian's first appearance at a race, not every WAG is quite as friendly towards her as Alexandra just yet - not that they think there is much they can do to dim the star power of one of the world's most famous celebrities.

Kim Kardashian kisses Lewis Hamilton on his luxury yacht after attending the Monaco GP

Kardashian's first Formula One race left many of her fellow WAGs split over her presence

But she didn't have a care in the world as she fell into the arms of her F1-racer boyfriend

She was joined on the yacht by her sister Khloe, who had joined her for the race in France

An insider on the F1 circuit said: 'There is a sense that she is stealing the show.

'There was a sense of jealousy when Kim arrived because the other ladies are used to pulling focus. However, she doesn’t let it bother her. She’s used to it and knows the value she is bringing to the game.

Call me evil.. but I'm exposing Serena Williams Hi. I'm columnist Liz Jones, and if no one else is willing to admit the sleazy truth about Serena Williams's sudden return to tennis, I will. The American is set to make her much-hyped return to professional tennis today. But her return is undignified - and the worst possible example for girls. I hope she crashes out. Click here to read my piece

'She doesn’t really care if the other girls don’t like her, but some of their teams have reached out to arrange lunches. She's open, but is focused on Lewis.'

A different source said: 'F1 is already a world filled with enormous wealth, big personalities and even bigger egos. Now that Kim is part of that scene and expected to be around more often, the reaction has been mixed.

'Some people couldn't care less and are focused on their own circles, while others see value in being close to her because of the access and influence that can come with it.'

The exchange with Brundle, however, has been seen as a misstep in the circles where Kardashian is trying to become more familiar.

Brundle, a former driver, is now famed within the global F1 fanbase for his pre-race walkabouts where he interviews celebrities on the fly on the grid in the minutes before a race begins.

He noticed Kim and sister Khloe and approached them while on live TV. Both looked at him and turned away before seemingly encouraging their entourage to try and forcefully move him along.

'Things shifted once word spread about her interaction - or lack of one - with Martin Brundle,' the second insider continued. 'Among many of the regulars in the F1 paddock, it was viewed as a pretty classless moment.

'The real question now is what happens the next time she's at a race. There will definitely be more eyes on her, and some feel she's become an unnecessary distraction at an event that, ideally, should be about the racing rather than the celebrity surrounding it.

The 45-year-old headed out to Hamilton's yacht after he finished second in the race

She was clearly proud and impressed as Hamilton finished runner-up at the glitzy race

Some were furious at Kardashian's 'classless' interaction with F1 reporter Martin Brundle

Observers said Kardashian's incident with Brundle was also a bad look for Hamilton, too

Kardashian joined fellow Ferrari WAG Alexandra Leclerc to watch the race in Monaco

'And it's also not a great look for Lewis by association.'

Hamilton's reputation has been another key talking point here. A seven-time world champion, the Brit is desperately pursuing one more championship to edge Michael Schumacher and become the most decorated driver in the history of the sport.

But his last world title was in 2020 and he trails runaway leader Kimi Antonelli by a huge 66 points in the driver's standings this time around.

With that eighth title still far off, some have pondered whether his high-profile romance with Kardashian has helped him recapture some of the allure that his profile has lost in recent years.

Sources told Daily Mail that some F1 WAGs are desperate to be friendly with Kardashian

But many are now eager to see how she handles the attention on her next race appearance

After celebrating with Hamilton, she also had time to reflect on a whirlwind day with her sister

Some have said that Hamilton relishes the extra attention that comes from dating Kardashian

'Whether fair or not, people are talking about him for different reasons, and that level of visibility certainly doesn't hurt,' the source added. 'Lewis isn't the dominant force on the track that he once was. Wins haven't come as frequently in recent years.

'Because of that, some people aren't necessarily questioning the relationship itself, but they are wondering what initially drew him to it.

'There's a belief among some in his world that being linked to someone as famous as Kim puts him back at the center of the conversation in a way that extends beyond racing.

'For years, Lewis commanded attention because of what he was accomplishing on the track.

'That's why many believe he'd have no issue with Kim being around the F1 world as much as she wants. The spotlight follows her everywhere, and by extension, it keeps plenty of attention on him as well.'

As the fallout continues, Hamilton heads to Barcelona this weekend for the next Grand Prix on Sunday, June 14.

Sports.title: History-making jockey receives 10-year ban after being found guilty of fixing races
Sports.content:
History-making jockey receives 10-year ban after being found guilty of fixing races

S’manga Khumalo became South Africa’s first black champion jockey and first black jockey to win the Durban July, Africa’s biggest horse race, but has now been banned

View 3 Images S'mango Khumalo; banned for ten years (Image: AFP via Getty Images)

History-making jockey S’manga Khumala has been banned from his sport for 10 years after being found guilty of race-fixing.

‌



Khumalo overcame a difficult childhood to become South Africa’s first black champion jockey, the first black jockey to win the Durban July, the biggest race in Africa, and rode in Britain when he represented his country in the 2014 Shergar Cup at Ascot.

‌



He had been raised in one of South Africa's most violent townships, KwaMashu in Durban, which was once labelled the country’s murder capital. He had no connection with horses until he was approached at school by a talent scout from South Africa’s jockey academy.

‌



Haydock racing fixtures cancelled due to hole in track but Tom Grennan gig set to go ahead READ MORE :

Once graduating, he rose through the ranks to ride more than 2,300 winners including 22 successes at Group 1 level. He was a charismatic figure, earning the nickname ‘Bling’ for his peroxide hair, crystal stud earrings and horseshoe-tattooed hand.

However, the 40-year-old was stood down in March this year by the National Horseracing Authority accused of corruption offences.

He was charged with three offences and pleaded guilty and was found guilty of improperly communicating inside information with an unauthorised individual, named Noor Iqbal that could be used for betting purposes.

‌



View 3 Images Khumalo became the first black jockey to win the Durban July, on Heavy Metal in 2013 (Image: Getty Images)

He also admitted receiving more than £5,000 from Iqbal in return for the information “and/or riding, or agreeing to ride, in a manner intended to affect the performance of a horse and/or the outcome of a race for betting purposes”.

A third charge alleged Khumalo had “dishonestly and intentionally” failed to ensure that his horse ran on its merits by restraining, failing to obtain the best possible placing or deviating from instructions. The charge related to races between October 2025 and February 2026.

‌



View 3 Images S'manga Khumalo at the 2014 Shergar Cup (Image: Hugh Routledge/Shutterstock)

Khumalo pleaded not guilty but was found guilty by the Inquiry Board which postponed determination of penalty for further consideration.

On Wednesday the board announced the cancellation of Khumalo’s licence with immediate effect.

Article continues below

The announcement said: “Mr Khumalo is precluded from applying for, renewing, holding, or being issued any jockey licence for a period of fifteen (15) years, commencing 23 March 2026, of which five (5) years are suspended for 15 years. Mr Khumalo has the right of appeal."

Sports.title: Anthony Joshua told one major factor is 'key' to him beating Tyson Fury
Sports.content:
Anthony Joshua told one major factor is 'key' to him beating Tyson Fury

Anthony Joshua and Tyson Fury are finally set to trade leather later this year, and a boxing icon has told 'AJ' exactly how he can topple his long-time rival

View Image Tyson Fury and Anthony Joshua are set to finally face off (Image: Getty Images)

Anthony Joshua's 'psychological edge' is the key to defeating Tyson Fury in their heavyweight showdown later this year.

‌



That is the view of former four weight world champion, Roy Jones Jr. After over a decade of trading barbs, Joshua and Fury are finally expected to go head-to-head in a mouthwatering all-British dust-up before Christmas.

‌



The two heavyweight icons signed to fight each other just days after Fury won his comeback bout against Arslanbek Makhmudov back in April. Joshua will return to the ring next month - taking on Kristian Prenga on July 25 in Jeddah, Saudi Arabia, while the 'Gypsy King' is also expected to have another tune-up fight before facing 'AJ.'

‌



With the historic clash edging closer, many within the world of boxing have started to offer their thoughts on how the bout will go. And boxing legend Jones Jr, recently gave his opinion on the matter. The 57-year-old believes 'AJ's' mentality could be the key to getting the outcome he craves against Fury.

FOLLOW OUR FIGHTING FB PAGE! Latest boxing and MMA news, analysis and much more via our dedicated Facebook page

Tyson Fury picks his side in bitter feud between Eddie Hearn and Dana White READ MORE :

Ricky Hatton's mum in tears as granddaughter dances during emotional tribute night READ MORE :

In an interview with BettingLounge, the American said: "You’re looking to see how his mental dominance works. If he’s mentally dominant, then you know he’s ready to go into a big fight. If he’s not mentally dominant, then he’s not ready for Tyson Fury. Mental dominance is the look you see on his face from round one until whatever round it takes to end it. I started dominating before the weigh-in.

‌



"My mental dominance set in before the weigh-in, and I tried to dominate all the way up until the last bell rang. Against Jake Paul, his dominance showed up at that last weigh-in, at that last press conference. His dominance finally showed up. I said, 'Now we’ve got something.' And it lasted throughout the night. So if it happens the same way this time, if his mental dominance shows up right away and it lasts to the end, then we know we’ve got something."

Joshua and Fury are expected to engage in an epic rivalry - which should see them meet twice in the ring. The first outing is due to be broadcast live on Netflix, with the rematch set for DAZN. And regardless of how the first meeting ends, Jones Jr has urged the Brits not to retire and put on a sequel for the ages.

Tommy Fury vs Eddie Hall fight time and how to watch READ MORE :

Rising star Adam Maca reveals inspiration from Albanian roots READ MORE :

"It depends, because what if it’s a very good fight, a very competitive fight, and it’s close? We all want to see it again," explained Jones Jr. "We’re going to want to see two out of three. But if somebody blasts somebody, or somebody completely dominates somebody, we’re just going to say, 'Okay, well, he was better than him.' We kind of thought that, but we didn’t know. Now we know, and that’s good. If it’s a great fight, we all want to see it again. If it’s a dominating performance by one guy or the other, we don’t have to see it again."

Article continues below

Touching on Joshua's return, Jones Jr insists it does not matter how 'AJ's' looks in his clash with Prenga, as long as it does not jeopardise the former two-time heavyweight champion's meeting with Fury. "Sometimes you’re only as good as your opponent, so we can’t judge him by this fight," he said.

"It’s a different outlook and a different mindset when you know you’re fighting a top guy than when you’re fighting a guy with a padded record. He may look good and knock the guy right out, or the guy may come in and fight above his head and make Joshua have to work for it. But at the end of the day, Joshua should still beat him, and it doesn’t matter how Joshua looks. We’ve been waiting for the Joshua-Fury fight for so long that we don’t care how Joshua looks. As long as he wins, let’s just get these two guys in front of each other.

Sports.title: Michael Vaughan concerned by Ben Stokes' behaviour as England captaincy hangs in balance
Sports.content:
Michael Vaughan concerned by Ben Stokes' behaviour as England captaincy hangs in balance

Ben Stokes could lose the captaincy of the England Test side after breaking team rules by going to a nightclub after their win over New Zealand with Gus Atkinson

View 3 Images Ben Stokes is waiting to discover his fate (Image: Philip Brown/Getty Images)

Michael Vaughan has backed Ben Stokes to keep the England captaincy but has revealed concerns about the all-rounder’s recent behaviour.

‌



With question marks lingering over the 35-year-old’s future, Stokes appears to be involved in a stand-off with the England and Wales Cricket Board following his role in a nightclub incident which also involved team-mate Gus Atkinson and Saracens rugby union player Totoa Auvaa.

‌



Suggestions that Stokes was ready to break his silence on social media on Tuesday – possibly relinquishing his leadership role, or even stepping away from England duty more permanently – came to nothing. The ECB will need to name a squad for the second Test soon, with training due to begin at the Kia Oval on Sunday, meaning a decision to stand the pair down for that game may come before anything more permanent.

‌



The Women’s T20 World Cup begins at Edgbaston on Friday, with England hosting Sri Lanka, and there is an eagerness at Lord’s to have some clarity before Nat Sciver-Brunt’s team take centre stage.

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! All the best sports news and much more on our dedicated Facebook page

Timeline of Ben Stokes incident with England cricket and rugby stars drinking together READ MORE :

Vaughan, the Ashes-winning skipper who led his country 51 times from 2003 to 2008, has stepped into the debate to suggest the end of Stokes’ tenure is not inevitable. “Yes, Ben Stokes broke a curfew. Yes, he made a mistake. But is that a sacking offence as England’s Test captain? I do not think so,” he wrote in The Telegraph.

‌



“Stokes has a lot of credit in the bank for all he has done for England as captain and all-rounder. There is no way that those making the big decisions at the England and Wales Cricket Board have the same credit in the bank.

“I do not see how you can tell Stokes he is not captain anymore just for going over the curfew by a couple of hours after a win. The ECB is hoping Stokes makes a decision on its behalf. But it has to be brave enough and strong enough to do what it thinks is right. If that is to sack him then fine, but I do not agree with that decision on this issue.

View 3 Images Michael Vaughan has given his take on the situation (Image: Gareth Copley/Getty Images)

‌



“A short suspension would be fine, but this is not a big enough incident over which to lose the captaincy.”

While Vaughan believes there is a way back, he also shared worries over how Stokes has handled himself in recent times, dating back to the winter’s ill-fated Ashes tour.

“He has not seemed right for a while. Over the past week, before this incident blew up, I sent a few messages to people around the England camp that I had concerns about Stokes,” Vaughan wrote.

‌



View 3 Images Ben Stokes and Gus Atkinson were involved in a nightclub incident in Chelsea (Image: News Images/NurPhoto/Shutterstock)

“In Australia, he was aggressive with people a couple of times after interviews. I have heard that he has not been shaking the hands of well-respected people in the game. It was odd at Lord’s that he did not come down to have his photograph taken with all the other England ex-captains as part of the 150th Lord’s Test celebrations. He does not seem to respect the past or other people doing their jobs.”

Stokes and Atkinson remain under investigation for a “breach of team protocols” after breaking a midnight curfew while celebrating their Test victory over New Zealand at Lord’s last Sunday. The episode has also been referred to the independent Cricket Regulator.

Article continues below

A confrontation involving Auvaa, one of several Saracens players seen drinking with members of the England team earlier in the evening, is understood to have resulted in a physical confrontation that led to a member of ECB security staff being struck. Saracens are also conducting a probe to establish the full facts of the incident.

Sports.title: Rugby star nominated for global award after FOUR YEARS without touching a ball
Sports.content:
Rugby star nominated for global award after FOUR YEARS without touching a ball

Fin Lloyd-Gilmour has been recognised for his performances on the HSCB SVNS circuit

View 2 Images Finley Lloyd-Gilmour of Great Britain during the HSBC SVNS Sevens World Championship

Fin Lloyd-Gilmour spent four years without touching a rugby ball because of a troublesome knee condition but is now back making shortlists for a prestigious World Rugby award and playing alongside a British & Irish Lion.

‌



In his first season with the GB sevens team, Lloyd-Gilmour was recognised as one of the three nominees for Men's SVNS Rookie of the Year award. He underlined why he made that select group in Bordeaux in the third leg of the World Championship events, where he played alongside Scotland and Lions winger Darcy Graham, who was going back to his sevens roots.

‌



Graham and Lloyd-Gilmour were both on the scoresheet as GB stunned overall champions South Africa in the group stages on their way to qualification for the quarter-finals – with Lloyd-Gilmour clinching the win with an extra-time try.

‌



It has been a whirlwind for the former Salisbury RFC youngster who was also part of the Bath youth set-up. Lloyd-Gilmour said: “It was a nice surprise to be nominated. The news came through when we were on the coach from Spain (the previous week GB played in Valladolid) into France, so one of the boys saw that the women's nominations got posted and we crowded round the phones, just to see whether my name would pop up.

“It was an amazing surprise to be within that group of boys and be up for the awards. There was a big eruption from the boys on the back of the coach when that came through.

“I was just relieved to finally step on the pitch this season. I’d been in the GB set-up the year before but didn’t manage to get my first cap that year. So that made the first run-out in Singapore a lot sweeter and I didn’t take any moment for granted, which hopefully translates to what you see on the pitch.”

‌



View 2 Images Finley Lloyd-Gilmour of Great Britain in action at the Hong Kong Sevens

Lloyd-Gilmour’s path to this point has been an unlikely one. His father was born in Papua New Guinea before spending much of his life in Queensland, Australia, even playing representative sevens for the Wallabies at Under-18s level.

Despite being an Aussie through and through, he was cheering on GB when the two sides met at the end of May in Spain, Lloyd-Gilmour scoring a try in a narrow defeat to the eventual champions. Beyond family ties, that support is also reward for remarkable resilience. Lloyd-Gilmour was diagnosed with osteochondritis dissecans at 17, a knee injury that kept him away from the game for four years partly also due to the Covid-19 pandemic.

‌



He explained: “I didn’t touch a ball for four years partially due to Covid and a backlog of surgeries. It took a while to get back. I went to Loughborough University and ended up playing there, it was a bit like (France lock) Thibaut Flament’s story, I was in the sixth team. I played about seven games tops over the course of my university career, partially due to Covid. I managed to get up to Loughborough Uni thirds.

“To go through the sort of prolonged wait for surgery and the rehabilitation phase, it made me realise the love I have for the game and how much I missed being on the pitch with your mates left and right of you. I was always dedicated to coming back and trying to play rugby in any shape or format.

“I’m glad I stuck at it and persevered, to get to where I am. I certainly didn’t have international rugby on the radar but it’s one of the many good surprises that have come from coming back.”

‌



Football game with stars highlights Britain’s poor paternity deal for new fathers READ MORE :

Lloyd-Gilmour and GB impressed in Bordeaux in reaching the quarterfinals where they were beaten by New Zealand, who made it all the way to the final only to lose to Olympic champions and hosts France.

One of those New Zealanders, Kele Lasaqa, was rewarded with the Rookie of the Year crown ahead of Lloyd-Gilmour but simply making the top three capped off a remarkable debut season.

World Rugby CEO Alan Gilpin said: “The HSBC SVNS Awards recognise the exceptional talent, commitment and performances that have defined another outstanding year of rugby sevens around the world. From season-long standout performers to exciting new players making their mark on the international stage, these nominees represent the very best of our sport.”

Article continues below

After 12 events across HSBC SVNS, SVNS 2 and SVNS 3, just one tournament remains in Bordeaux (5th-7th June) as excitement builds to a season-ending crescendo, after which the HSBC SVNS World Champions 2026 will be crowned. For more information, please visit www.svns.com . Fans in the UK can catch every match live on Rugby Pass.

Sports.title: ‘That is the beauty of the Lions’ - Wales stars backed to feature on inaugural New Zealand Tour
Sports.content:
‘That is the beauty of the Lions’ - Wales stars backed to feature on inaugural New Zealand Tour

Former Wales captain Siwan Lillicrap believes a “handful” of Welsh players could force their way into the inaugural Lions Women’s Tour in 2027, despite a challenging Women’s Six Nations campaign

View Image “Two teams in Wales have already received the award for the last two years in Caernarfon and Ynysddu, the impact that money will have on those grassroots club is huge."

Wales might be enduring a tough time of it in the Women’s Six Nations but former skipper Siwan Lillicrap is adamant a handful of Welsh players will make it onto the inaugural Lions Women’s Tour in 2027.

Sean Lynn’s side suffered a second successive whitewash in 2026 as they dealt with a raft of injuries while bringing through a new generation of young players.

Lillicrap knows those up-and-comers better than most as head coach of Wales Under-18s, with a trio of 19-year-olds, forwards Jorja Aiono and Branwen Metcalfe, and scrum-half Seren Lockwood, all graduating to feature in every game of the 2026 Guinness Women’s Six Nations. Whether they can do enough to earn selection under Jo Yapp, named last week as the first Lions Women’s head coach, is another matter, but Lillicrap believes there is no limit to their potential, citing England men’s youngster Henry Pollock as an example to follow.

“Even though Wales maybe are in this transitional phase, with lots of youngsters playing, that is the beauty of the Lions Tour. You look at Henry Pollock in the men’s space, we are maybe seeing some young gems coming through in the women’s space, in Wales and other nations,” said Lillicrap, who is an ambassador for Royal London, founding partner of The British & Irish Lions Women’s rugby team.

“They have had some exposure during the Women’s Six Nations, Jorja Aiono, for example, played U18s last year and then started every game of this Six Nations campaign for Wales and has shown glimpses of potential world class ability and she is still only 19. You’ve also got Branwen Metcalfe and Seren Lockwood, all those girls were U18s last year.

“I knew they had star quality in them and knew they were the ultimate professionals. I worked with them for a couple of years before they got their senior caps and saw how they handled themselves in the day-to-day environment.

“The exciting bit for me is they are only 18 or 19 now so you are just seeing a glimpse now but where are they going to be in a few years’ time? You look at not this Lions Tour – although maybe, we’ve seen the Henry Pollock example – but in five years’ time, when the next Lions Tour is, what level with they be at with the provisions in place?”

Content cannot be displayed without consent

If selection to take on the Black Ferns in New Zealand will take even greater development from the trio, who have already taken to international rugby with ease, Lillicrap believes there are some established Test stars in the Welsh ranks who would be strong candidates to tour.

Alex Callender has captained Wales in recent times but missed the Six Nations through injury, while Keira Bevan and Sisilia Tuipulotu have shown time and again that they can compete with the best of the Red Roses at club level in Premiership Women’s Rugby.

Lillicrap added: “Maybe the team hasn’t had the results they would have liked in this transitional phase but you have experienced players who have missed out this year like Alex Callender due to injury, she’s an outstanding player, in my opinion, possibly the best seven in the world potentially with the amount of work she gets through.

“You’ve got Sisilia Tuipulotu who is still only young, she has got a ton of caps under her belt. Her raw ability is fantastic. And then you have one of Wales’s most experienced players is Keira Bevan, you’ve seen quality performances from her against England so there is star quality and experience in the team.

“The beauty of the Lions is that it might not be 20 Welsh girls there but I expect a handful of Welsh girls and there is still so much to play for.”

As well as supporting the inaugural Lions Tour, Royal London have demonstrated their commitment to the grassroots game with their annual Championing Women and Girls’ Grassroots Rugby Award. The initiative, in its third year, recognises four clubs per year, one chosen from each Union (England, Ireland, Scotland and Wales), who will receive a trophy plus a £10,000 grant to invest in their women and girls' programmes. Applications are open until 12pm on Monday 20 July 2026 via the Lions website.

And having seen how the likes of previous recipients Caernarfon RFC and Ynysddu have used their grants, Lillicrap is urging more clubs to get involved. She added: “Two teams in Wales have already received the award for the last two years in Caernarfon and Ynysddu, the impact that money will have on those grassroots club is huge.

“Clubs are using it for various different things, developing young women’s referees in Caernarfon for example and in Ynysddu, they are using it to ensure everyone has accessibility to games, so there are no limiting factors.

Article continues below

“The money essentially breaks down any barriers that women and girls have. Hopefully lots of clubs apply for it because £10,000 is significant and can make a positive change for your environment.”

Royal London, the only Founding Partner of The British & Irish Lions Women’s rugby team, has announced that applications are open for its annual Championing Women and Girls’ Rugby Award. Applications are open until 12pm on Monday 20 July 2026 via the Lions website

Sports.title: World Cup team forced to release statement after footage emerges of arrival into US
Sports.content:
World Cup team forced to release statement after footage emerges of arrival into US

Footage emerged of the team appearing to be searched on the airport tarmac during their journey to the World Cup, but a statement has now been released clarifying the pictures

View Image Senegal has released a statement on their arrival in the USA for the World Cup. (Image: Matt McNulty - FIFA/FIFA via Getty Images)

The Senegal Football Federation has released a statement clarifying the situation surrounding their arrival in the USA for the World Cup. Footage emerged online appearing to show players and staff members being screened and searched on the airport tarmac.

‌



The videos prompted widespread criticism online. Among those to take aim at the footage was former England striker and pundit Ian Wright.

‌



The incident came at a similar time as when Somali referee Omar Artan was denied entry to the country. He was turned away after an 11-hour-long interview at border control.

‌



Senegal have now moved to explain the situation, clarifying that the checks actually took place before the team’s arrival in San Antonio. They also explain that the checks were pre-arranged.

“Following the circulation on social media of a video showing players and staff members of the Senegal national team undergoing a security check on an airport tarmac, we wish to provide the following clarifications in order to avoid any erroneous interpretation,” the statement read.

England vs Costa Rica: 5 questions Thomas Tuchel needs to answer before the World Cup READ MORE :

Jamie Vardy makes decision on returning to Leicester City and confirms retirement plan READ MORE :

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

‌



“Contrary to certain reported information, this check did not take place upon the team's arrival in San Antonio, but rather at the time of boarding at Raleigh airport on Sunday, June 7, 2026, before the flight's departure.

“As part of the logistical organisation of the trip, the bus carrying the national team left the hotel in Raleigh to go directly onto the airport tarmac.

"This procedure allowed the players and staff members to complete all security and police checks directly at the foot of the aircraft, without having to pass through the usual areas of the terminal and the boarding lounges.

‌



“This arrangement was essentially aimed at optimising the travel time of the delegation and facilitating its boarding on the private flight to San Antonio.

Content cannot be displayed without consent

“We wish to emphasise that this procedure took place in compliance with the airport security rules in force and that no particular incident was reported.

‌



“The private flight connecting Raleigh to San Antonio took place under excellent conditions, and the entire delegation arrived at its destination normally.”

Senegal were in action in the early hours of the morning as they drew 0-0 with Saudi Arabia. The game saw Chelsea striker Nicolas Jackson receive a red card. The nation takes on France, Norway and Iraq in their group stage games.

Sports.title: Man Utd transfer target Karl Darlow in talks over new contract with Leeds
Sports.content:
Man Utd transfer target Karl Darlow in talks over new contract with Leeds

Manchester United have shown an interest in signing Karl Darlow this summer, but Leeds are determined to keep the 35-year-old goalkeeper and have opened talks

View 2 Images Karl Darlow performed superbly during the second half of last season (Image: Nathan Stirk/Getty Images)

Leeds United are currently in negotiations with goalkeeper Karl Darlow, whose contract expires at the end of the month.

‌



The 35-year-old has attracted interest from several Premier League clubs over the past month, including Manchester United, who are searching for an experienced back-up goalkeeper. United have extended the contract of Tom Heaton, 40, for another season, yet have also looked at Darlow and Wolves' Sam Johnstone.

‌



Darlow could leave Leeds - where he has made 38 appearances in three years - as a free agent at the end of June. United have Senne Lammens established as their No.1 and Heaton retained, but have a goalkeeping department in a state of flux, with Altay Bayindir on the transfer list and Andre Onana also available for a permanent move away after a loan spell at Trabzonspor.

‌



However, Leeds are determined to retain Darlow, who played a key role in helping the Whites steer clear of relegation last season, reports Leeds Live.

FOLLOW OUR MAN UTD FB PAGE! Latest United news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Man Utd officially confirm Jadon Sancho and five other players will leave the club READ MORE :

The Wales international displaced summer signing Lucas Perri as first choice in January, going on to record five clean sheets in 22 Premier League appearances while producing a string of impressive saves — one of which, against Wolves, earned a nomination for save of the season.

‌



The shot-stopper has begun each of his three campaigns under Daniel Farke as second choice, yet in the last two has ultimately finished the season as the number one. The manager suggested last month that he was eager to hold on to Darlow.

Nevertheless, Leeds are expected to dip into the goalkeeper market again this summer, and it remains possible that Darlow — who has 38 club appearances to his name — could find himself earmarked for a back-up role once more. Farke hinted back in January that he had a particular preference in mind for a goalkeeper signing.

View 2 Images Senne Lammens will stay as Manchester United's No.1 goalkeeper (Image: Mark Cosgrove/News Images/NurPhoto via Getty Images)

‌



Meanwhile, Michael Carrick's side have confirmed that Jadon Sancho, Casemiro and Tyrell Malacia will leave the club this summer upon the expiry of their contracts. The club announced on Wednesday morning that Sonny Aljofree, James Bailey and Malachi Sharpe would also depart when their deals ran out.

After finishing third and securing a place in the Champions League next season, United are eager to reshape their squad this summer. A top-class midfielder to replace the outgoing Casemiro is the priority, with Atalanta's Ederson poised to be the first signing of the summer window.
